inherits.scope: exact same two repository-derived registered fault injections, public/hidden cases, full and structured interfaces; v1 remains immutable

models.routing_scope: requested selector only; provider weights and routing not independently attested

selection_policy: All three preregistered models receive all four fixed task/arm cells. No capability-based model selection, replacement or winner-only reporting. Two local sizes are one family, not independent families.

generation.decoder: generic JSON object syntax only; identical for both arms

codex.output_budget_enforcement: Conservative output+reasoning proxy checked at completion; reasoning is an output detail so this can reject below 2048 actual output tokens. Over-budget answers are rejected and actual input/output/cache/reasoning retained separately. CLI protocol exposes no local-engine hard n_predict bound. Both arms use the identical preregistered proxy.
codex.context_policy: Extra CLI system context and cached input tokens are recorded as actual provider usage. They are not removed to make local/API input counts look equal.
codex.decoder: strict whole JSON candidate parser after response; no grammar claim for the API
codex.request_policy: Fresh owned ephemeral read-only CLI for each response with full public history; all tool or unregistered events reject; existing user rules remain effective.
codex.allowed_non_answer_items: Only typed reasoning text with id/type/text fields within the sole active turn. Reasoning items cannot be candidates or tool calls; their count and actual reported reasoning tokens are retained.
codex.usage_semantics: input_tokens and output_tokens are the reported total components; cached_input_tokens is input detail, reasoning_output_tokens is output detail. Actual reported total=input+output. output+reasoning remains a conservative admission-budget proxy and is not labeled actual total.

cohort_order: Fixed model order; within each model task order inherited from v1 and arms rotate by task index. Sequential execution only. One local engine may serve multiple cells with cache_prompt=false; startup, restart, final identity and shutdown wall are shared equally between arms, by a rule fixed before requests.
availability_policy: Reprobe the actual CLI in the current environment and retain raw result. Historical usage-limit evidence remains historical. Available means no benchmark task was yet attempted; provider failures during the cohort remain unavailable/incomplete, not incorrect answers.
failure_policy: A timeout or incomplete local transport ends that cell; retain unknown usage and close/reap its engine. After confirmed cleanup, continue the next distinct cell with a fresh engine; no retry of that failed cell. Provider unavailability ends that provider cohort; uncertainty about process ownership/cleanup stops the study. Public candidate rejection alone permits the second registered response. Hidden evaluation is terminal. Compiler, linker, file/runtime and native timeout failures are infrastructure outcomes with retained stage/raw evidence; they do not become candidate feedback or buy a second attempt.
cost_policy: Per model report exact observed task usage including cached/provider reasoning fields, all request/wall and validation/retry costs. Model noncell hash/startup/restart/shutdown wall is divided equally between arms; campaign source/admission/aggregation wall is divided across three planned models then arms. Each arm also bears one full native controls campaign and its corresponding model/runtime acquisition receipt service wall. Codex additionally itemizes the full availability probe wall and usage. These standalone-arm acquisition allocations are not summed as actual elapsed campaign time; downloaded models overlapped. Task token-per-success excludes the separately retained availability probe. External process receipt covers interpreter startup and final serialization. No cross-provider token-to-money pooling or price claim.
